name: RAPGEF5
summary: RAPGEF5, on chromosome 4. A nonsense variant, c.2624C>A (p.Ser875*; g.54108297G>T on EquCab 3.0), truncates the protein and causes equine familial isolated hypoparathyroidism (EFIH), formerly called idiopathic hypocalcaemia: a Thoroughbred foal that cannot regulate its blood calcium and dies young. It is recessive; carriers show no signs, and colts and fillies are affected alike. It has been found only in Thoroughbreds, at a low allele frequency of about 0.8 per cent in a United States survey, after a first estimate of 1.8 per cent. UC Davis writes the genotypes N/N, N/EFIH and EFIH/EFIH. No effect on coat, build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: RAPGEF5 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is clinically normal and passes the copy to half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Hypoparathyroidism (EFIH)
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The foal cannot keep its blood calcium up: parathyroid hormone is low, or only normal when it should be high, and phosphorus is raised. Signs appear early, reported up to about 35 days old: sustained muscle contractions, a stiff gait, seizures, fever, a fast heart rate, lying down and finally being unable to stand. It is invariably fatal.
